title: Admin/agent APIs unauthenticated by default (DESK_API_KEY empty), even in production

DESK_API_KEY is absent from .env.example, docker-compose.dev.yml and k8s/helm/values.yaml, so the documented deployment path leaves every /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/agents/* route open. title: Unauthenticated webchat WebSocket: guessable visitor_id is the only credential; connecting hijacks the conversation
root_cause: /ws/chat/{visitor_id} has no authentication or session binding. WebChatManager.connect (lines 59-75) closes any previously registered socket for the id and registers the new one. The bundled widget (static/webchat.html:76) generates visitor_id as 'widget-' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,10) (~41 bits, non-cryptographic PRNG); ids are logged at info on every connect. Nothing rate-limits connection attempts (the limiter only counts frames after connect).
failure_scenario: Attacker who learns/guesses an active visitor_id opens WS /ws/chat/<victim_id>: the victim's live socket is closed, all subsequent AI/agent replies (healthcare/legal/fintech PII for the target market) are pushed to the attacker, and the attacker can inject messages as the victim into the same persisted conversation.
suggested_fix: Issue a signed short-lived session token via HTTP and validate it on WS connect; generate visitor ids server-side with secrets.token_urlsafe (or crypto.randomUUID client-side); never displace a live socket with an unauthenticated one; rate-limit connection attempts per IP. Merged with API-batch finding on Math.random ids.

title: Raw conversation history bypasses PII Shield on frontier-routed turns
root_cause: process_detailed runs PII detection/redaction only on the current inbound content (line 225). conversation_history is passed verbatim into build_prompt_with_persona (lines 339-343). MessageProcessor._load_history (workers/message_processor.py:260-264) builds history from msg.content (raw), never the persisted content_redacted column; PromptBuilder._format_history interpolates it unchanged.
failure_scenario: Frontier enabled. Turn 1 contains a phone number -> routed LOCAL. Turn 2 has no PII and complexity >= 0.6 -> FRONTIER: the OpenAI prompt contains the raw prior turn with the phone number. Same leak on REDACTED_FRONTIER_OK turns. The core sovereignty guarantee is defeated for history even when the shield works perfectly on the current message.
suggested_fix: When the routing target is frontier-bound, load content_redacted for history (or re-run pii_shield.analyze on each historical customer turn and substitute redacted_text). Apply the same gate consistently to the Vault query path.

title: Multi-participant email threads collide on the global conversation unique constraint: permanent 500s and message loss
root_cause: compute_thread_id anchors every reply on References[0]/In-Reply-To (thread root), so all participants produce the same channel_conversation_id. get_or_create_conversation (conversations/manager.py:72-107) looks up scoped to customer_id but the model enforces a GLOBAL UniqueConstraint('channel','channel_conversation_id') (models/conversation.py:106-110). Different From addresses resolve to different customers, so the second participant's INSERT violates the constraint. MessageRouter.route catches IntegrityError only around add_message (message_router.py:98-113), not conversation creation.
failure_scenario: Customer A starts thread X; CC'd colleague B replies with References: X. B resolves as a different customer; customer-scoped lookup misses; INSERT hits uq_conversations_channel_conversation_id -> unhandled IntegrityError -> 500. The relay retries on 500 and fails identically forever: B's messages are never persisted or answered.
suggested_fix: Make thread identity consistent: either look up by (channel, channel_conversation_id) without the customer filter, or change the constraint to (customer_id, channel, channel_conversation_id) and make the thread key participant-aware. Catch IntegrityError in get_or_create_conversation and re-read the winning row. Confirmed by two independent reviewers.

title: Outbound delivery failures silently lost: no retry or delivery tracking; both callers ignore the failure result
root_cause: OutboundDispatcher's docstring claims retry logic and delivery tracking, but dispatch() makes exactly one adapter.send() attempt and converts any failure into {'success': False} with no retry, backoff, dead-letter or persisted delivery status. workers/message_processor.py:144 discards the result and acks the event (lines 147-152); agents/inbox_api.py:394-428 only logs delivery and still returns success=True to the agent.
failure_scenario: Graph API 401/429/5xx, SMTP reset, or visitor socket mid-send: dispatch returns success=False; the processor acks anyway; the inbox endpoint reports success. The customer never receives the reply, the conversation shows as answered, and nothing records or retries the failed delivery.
suggested_fix: Implement bounded retry with backoff (or a delivery outbox), persist per-message delivery status, and make callers check result['success']: on failure dead-letter/mark undelivered and surface in the inbox instead of acking as done. Merges three reviewer findings (dispatcher, processor, inbox endpoint).

title: Routing event published before DB commit; webhook 200 sent before commit — commit failure loses the message permanently
root_cause: route() publishes conversation.routed to Redis inside the request transaction, before any commit. get_db (db.py:82-92) commits after yield; with FastAPI >= 0.111 (requirements.txt:2) that teardown runs after the 200 response is sent. No transactional outbox links publish to commit.
failure_scenario: Webhook routes a message, publish succeeds, 200 is sent to Meta, then commit fails (connection drop, deadlock). Meta never redelivers; the inbound row rolls back; the processor finds no conversation, _wait_for_visible_conversation gives up, and the orphan event is acked. The customer message is lost with no trace beyond logs.
suggested_fix: Use a transactional outbox (persist event row in the same transaction, publish after commit via relay), or at minimum commit before publishing and before returning the webhook response, returning non-2xx on commit failure so providers redeliver.

title: No pending-entry recovery: messages read but not acked are stranded forever (at-least-once not implemented)
root_cause: subscribe() only reads new entries via XREADGROUP '>'. No XPENDING/XAUTOCLAIM/XCLAIM exists anywhere; the worker uses a fixed consumer_name 'processor-1' (message_processor.py:61) shared across replicas. Entries delivered but never XACKed stay in the PEL indefinitely. Malformed-entry 'continue' guards (lines 99-109) also leave entries pending forever.
failure_scenario: Worker reads a batch then is killed (OOM, deploy, cancellation) before acking. After restart, '>' returns only newer entries; stranded events are never reprocessed — those customers never receive an AI reply and the events never reach the DLQ.
suggested_fix: On startup and periodically, XAUTOCLAIM idle pending entries with a min-idle-time and reprocess, with a delivery-count cap routing poison entries to the DLQ. Use unique consumer names per process (hostname+pid).

title: Production CMD runs 4 uvicorn workers but webchat delivery, runtime settings and SLA scanning are per-process
root_cause: CMD uses --workers 4. Each worker's lifespan starts its own MessageProcessor (main.py:119-124) consuming the same Redis group 'ai-processors' with identical consumer_name 'processor-1', so events load-balance across workers. WebChatManager.active_connections and the agent WS registry are process-local dicts with no cross-process pub/sub; WebChatAdapter.send returns success=True/delivered=False when the socket lives elsewhere (webchat.py:173-189). runtime_settings._overrides is per-process; Helm replicaCount: 2 has the same problem.

title: Rate limiter state grows without bound: attacker-controlled visitor keys never evicted (memory-exhaustion DoS)
root_cause: _events is a defaultdict(deque) keyed by unauthenticated client-supplied visitor_id. _prune() pops expired timestamps but leaves the empty deque and dict key; allow() creates a key for every unseen visitor. reset() has zero production callers; no periodic sweep, TTL or size cap. Process-wide singleton.
failure_scenario: Attacker sequentially opens WS connections with unique ids, sends one frame each, disconnects. Entries survive forever; a few hundred thousand cheap connections retain hundreds of MB, eventually OOM-killing the single process serving all channels. The abuse-mitigation component itself becomes the DoS vector.
suggested_fix: Delete keys whose deque becomes empty in _prune; add a periodic sweep or LRU cap; rate-limit connection attempts per IP at the webchat endpoint so key creation is throttled.

title: WS API key accepted via ?token= query parameter (logged in URLs)

title: Shared Desk API key persisted in localStorage and auto-replayed on page load
root_cause: saveCreds/loadCreds store desk-console-key (the shared DESK_API_KEY, admin-capable when paired with the role header outside production) in localStorage; init() auto-connects with it on every visit.

title: few_shot_examples dicts rendered as Python repr into the system prompt

title: Audit-logs 'total' is the page size, not the matching row count

title: contacts[0] profile name applied to every message in a batch misattributes customer display names
root_cause: parse_inbound_message reads profile_name once from value['contacts'][0] and assigns it as sender_name to ALL messages in value['messages'] (418). Meta batches messages from multiple senders with a parallel contacts array; the code never matches contact to message by wa_id.

suggested_fix: Build a wa_id -> profile.name map from value['contacts'] and look up each message's sender (message_data['from']), falling back to None.

title: Signed-but-malformed webhook body raises unhandled JSON errors (500 instead of 400), inviting redelivery loops
root_cause: After signature verification, payload = await request.json() is unwrapped: a signed but invalid-JSON body (or a JSON list, so payload.get('entry') raises AttributeError) propagates as 500. Meta/BSPs retry on any non-2xx.
failure_scenario: A misconfigured BSP proxy forwards a corrupted body: Desk 500s on JSONDecodeError/AttributeError and the provider redelivers the same poison payload repeatedly (Meta retries up to 7 days) — sustained 500s instead of a single terminal 400.
suggested_fix: Wrap request.json() in try/except ValueError and validate isinstance(payload, dict); raise HTTPException(400) for malformed payloads so providers stop redelivering.

title: Fresh UUID fallback for missing Message-ID defeats relay-redelivery deduplication
root_cause: build_inbound_message uses message_id = msg.message_id or f'email-{uuid.uuid4().hex}'. MessageRouter's idempotency keys on channel_message_id, so mail without a Message-ID gets a brand-new id on every delivery attempt and is never recognized as a duplicate.
failure_scenario: An automated sender omitting Message-ID posts mail via the relay; Desk commits and routes, but the response times out at the relay. Redelivery generates a new uuid, dedup misses, and the message is persisted and AI-answered a second time — duplicate replies for one email.
suggested_fix: Derive a deterministic fallback id from stable content (sha256 of from+to+subject+body+Date) so redeliveries collide on channel_message_id and are deduplicated.

title: Customer PII (recipient addresses, subjects, query text) logged at INFO across channels

Subjects routinely carry sensitive context ('Re: your HIV lab results').

suggested_fix: Log hashed/truncated recipients, omit subjects, and log only a hash/length of Vault queries (the cache key already uses SHA-256) or gate content logging behind an explicit debug flag. Merges two reviewer findings.

title: messages_sent health counter incremented before/regardless of delivery outcome

title: initialize() can create duplicate license_state rows; later reads pick arbitrarily
root_cause: initialize does SELECT ... LIMIT 1 (no ORDER BY) and inserts a default row when none found, with no singleton constraint and no locking. Two concurrent initializers both see zero rows and both insert.
failure_scenario: Two concurrent first requests after deployment create two license_state rows; activate_license updates whichever row LIMIT 1 returns while another process reads the other — tier/status diverge across the deployment and gates behave inconsistently.
suggested_fix: Enforce a singleton (unique constant column or fixed primary key) with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, or an advisory lock during initialization; order reads deterministically.

title: verify_audit_chain is unreachable and loads the entire audit table into memory
root_cause: No endpoint, task or test invokes verify_audit_chain (grep-verified), so tamper-evidence is never actually checked. When called it SELECTs every AuditLog row (unbounded, ever-growing) into a Python list.

suggested_fix: Expose verification via an admin endpoint/background job; verify incrementally (keyset pagination or periodic checkpoint hashes) instead of loading all rows.

title: Retention sweep issues per-conversation deletes plus a chain-head SELECT per audit entry in one long transaction
root_cause: The loop executes one DELETE for messages, one ORM delete, and one log_audit_event (which itself SELECTs the latest audit row) per conversation, all before a single commit at 239.
failure_scenario: A first run after months of accumulation with thousands of expired conversations produces tens of thousands of sequential round-trips in one transaction — long-running locks on messages/conversations/audit_logs blocking inbound routing and other audit writers.
suggested_fix: Batch deletes (DELETE ... WHERE conversation_id IN (SELECT ... LIMIT batch)), commit per batch, and write one aggregate audit entry per batch.

title: Span stack is a mutable list shared across copied contexts, corrupting parenting under concurrency
root_cause: _span_stack stores a list object in a ContextVar; child tasks (anyio task groups used by BaseHTTPMiddleware, asyncio.gather/create_task) inherit a context copy referencing the SAME list. start_span appends and Span.end removes on this shared list without isolation.
failure_scenario: Two concurrent operations within one request each start spans on the same list; when the first ends, stack.remove pops it and a subsequent span from the still-running second operation is parented to the wrong active span — mis-parented trace trees; out-of-order ends leave stale spans.
suggested_fix: Store an immutable tuple in the ContextVar and set a new tuple on push/pop (copy-on-write) so each copied context gets its own stack while preserving parent inheritance.

title: Client-supplied X-Trace-Id accepted without validation and bound into every log line
root_cause: TraceIdMiddleware uses request.headers.get(TRACE_HEADER) verbatim (any length/charset) as the structlog trace_id and echoes it on the response; no format/length check.
failure_scenario: A client sends a multi-kilobyte or log-forgery X-Trace-Id (spaces, quotes, key=value sequences): every structlog line during the request carries it, amplifying log volume and injecting misleading fields into log parsers.
suggested_fix: Validate against a strict pattern (^[a-f0-9]{32}$ or bounded [A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}) and generate a fresh id when it does not match.

title: confidence_threshold of 0.0 silently ignored (truthiness check)
root_cause: 'if cfg.confidence_threshold:' treats 0.0 as falsy. PUT /config/ai allows confidence_threshold=0.0 (admin/api.py:245, ge=0.0) and persists it, but the engine never applies a zero threshold.
failure_scenario: Admin sets confidence_threshold=0 to disable confidence-based escalation; the value is persisted and echoed by GET /config/ai but the engine keeps the previous scorer/threshold — the setting is silently ineffective.
suggested_fix: Use 'if cfg.confidence_threshold is not None:' so 0.0 is applied like any other valid threshold.

title: PII write-back targets the newest customer message, not the message being processed
root_cause: The write-back selects the latest customer message by created_at desc, id desc (Message.id is a random UUID, so the tie-break is arbitrary) rather than the specific message that triggered this pipeline run. The router persists inbound messages in the API process while the worker handles events asynchronously, so a newer message can exist by write-back time.
failure_scenario: Customer rapidly sends A (PII) then B (no PII); the processor handles A after B is persisted -> A's pii_detected/pii_types/content_redacted are written onto B's row; B's own processing overwrites them with B's no-PII result. A's row is never flagged: the inbox shows the wrong message redacted and loses A's PII audit trail.
suggested_fix: Pass the inbound message id through the routed event/pipeline and UPDATE ... WHERE id = :message_id instead of re-selecting the newest customer message.

title: create_outbound_message cast hides channel values rejected by OutboundMessage (e.g. 'mock')
root_cause: The local ChannelType Literal and typing.cast perform no runtime validation; OutboundMessage's pydantic channel Literal (schemas/channels.py:67-69) excludes 'mock'. run_processor registers MockChannelAdapter with channel_type='mock' (message_processor.py:338-345), so mock-channel events carry channel='mock'.
failure_scenario: A message arrives via the mock adapter: create_outbound_message constructs OutboundMessage(channel='mock') -> pydantic ValidationError -> _persist_and_build_outbound raises -> the processor dead-letters the event and the mock conversation never receives a reply.
suggested_fix: Add 'mock' to the OutboundMessage channel Literal (dev adapter) or validate/normalize the channel against the schema before construction instead of casting.

title: No character/token budget on conversation history; long conversations overflow local model context
root_cause: _format_history caps message COUNT (max_context_messages=10) but not total characters. Knowledge is budgeted (max_knowledge_chars=2000) while history is not; webchat inbound content is capped at 10000 chars per message (schemas/api.py:67), so 10 prior turns can contribute ~100KB of prompt text.
failure_scenario: A long webchat conversation with several near-max-length messages produces a >100KB prompt; the local Ollama/vLLM endpoint rejects it for exceeding context length -> provider.generate raises -> canned fallback_reply. Precisely the longest, most context-dependent conversations systematically fail to get real answers.
suggested_fix: Add a total history character/token budget (truncate or drop oldest turns to fit, analogous to max_knowledge_chars), sized to the local model's context window minus knowledge/system/current-message allowances.

title: Dev tooling shipped in the production image
root_cause: requirements.txt mixes runtime and dev dependencies (pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov, mypy, ruff, black, isort, pre-commit) and both Dockerfiles install the whole file into the final image; pyproject already separates these into [project.optional-dependencies].dev.
failure_scenario: The production image carries test/lint tooling and transitive dependencies, enlarging image size and attack surface (e.g. pre-commit's git hook machinery) for no runtime benefit.
suggested_fix: Split into runtime-only requirements (or install from pyproject main dependencies) plus a requirements-dev.txt used by CI/lint jobs.

title: Default migration URL points at port 5433, which no provided service exposes
root_cause: sqlalchemy.url defaults to postgresql+asyncpg://desk:desk@localhost:5433/desk while docker-compose.dev.yml maps Postgres to 5432 and .env.example uses 5432. The fallback is used when DATABASE_URL is unset.
failure_scenario: Developer runs alembic upgrade head without exporting DATABASE_URL (the compose flow sets it only inside the container): alembic tries localhost:5433, connection refused, migration fails confusingly.
suggested_fix: Change the default to localhost:5432 to match compose/.env.example, or remove the hardcoded URL and require DATABASE_URL.

title: MinIO image uses floating 'latest' tag
root_cause: image: minio/minio:latest is unpinned while postgres and redis are major-version pinned; MinIO has made breaking console/API changes across releases.
failure_scenario: A fresh docker compose pull months later fetches a new MinIO major with changed behavior/credentials handling, breaking the dev stack or silently changing stored-object semantics on an unchanged commit.
suggested_fix: Pin a specific MinIO release tag (e.g. minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-xx-xx).
verification_notes: Fixed in batch 14 (commit 62383a9) on branch fix/ocr-full-audit-round1. Verification: venv/bin/python -m ruff check src/desk/ -> exit 0; venv/bin/python -m mypy src/desk/ --ignore-missing-imports --python-version 3.14 -> Success, 0 errors; PYTHONPATH=src venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -m 'not e2e' -> 430 passed, 0 failed. Regression tests: tests/unit/test_review_round4_fixes.py (behavioral takeover tests), tests/e2e/test_message_flow.py.

title: Application image defaults to 'latest' with IfNotPresent
root_cause: image.tag 'latest' + pullPolicy IfNotPresent means nodes reuse whatever 'latest' they cached; CI publishes both :latest and :sha tags but the chart defaults to the mutable one.
failure_scenario: A helm upgrade after a new image push does not roll pods to the new code on nodes that cached 'latest'; different replicas can run different versions and rollbacks to a known-good build are impossible.
suggested_fix: Default the tag to the chart appVersion or require an immutable sha tag; use pullPolicy Always only with mutable tags.

title: SystemSetting model absent from Alembic target metadata; autogenerate would drop system_settings
root_cause: env.py imports desk.models.base, triggering desk/models/__init__.py registering the 10 core models — but SystemSetting is defined in desk/admin/runtime_settings.py and not imported there. target_metadata lacks the system_settings table that migration a7f3c2d91e05 creates.
failure_scenario: The next alembic revision --autogenerate compares metadata (no system_settings) against the DB (table exists) and emits op.drop_table('system_settings'), silently deleting all persisted admin runtime overrides if applied unreviewed.
suggested_fix: Import SystemSetting in desk/models/__init__.py (or import desk.admin.runtime_settings in env.py) so all tables register on Base.metadata. Note: low frequency but data-loss potential — review any autogenerated migration carefully.

title: SLA config test contains a no-op patch and a redundant duplicated assertion
root_cause: patch.object(ConversationManager, '_ensure_first_response_sla', ConversationManager._ensure_first_response_sla) replaces the method with itself (no effect), and 'assert 0 < -minutes or minutes < 0' has two identical disjuncts, suggesting a mistyped two-sided check. The real verification is only the following abs() assertion (302).
failure_scenario: No current false pass, but the no-op patch and duplicated disjunct mask intent: a future edit trusting the apparent rigor could weaken line 302 and leave the SLA window effectively unverified.
suggested_fix: Remove the self-patch; replace line 301 with a single clear assertion (assert minutes < 0) or drop it since 302 already bounds the value.

title: Smoke script's webhook signature is decorative — signed with a key the app never uses
root_cause: WEBHOOK_SECRET is hardcoded to 'dev_secret_key_change_me' (line 31) but the app verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 with WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET (default empty -> verification skipped in dev). The 'seed via signed webhook' step exercises no signature verification and only works against dev servers with verification disabled.
failure_scenario: Against a server with a real WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET: every seed POST is rejected 401 and the smoke run fails despite a healthy server. Against dev: the 'webhook accepted' check would pass even if HMAC verification were entirely broken.
suggested_fix: Read the signing secret from an env var (WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET) matching the target server; document that the script requires a dev server or a configured secret.
